case.brief: Scenario summary: You are the registered nurse conducting a scheduled home management review for Maya Okonkwo, a 30-year-old secondary school teacher who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes nine days ago and discharged from hospital seven days ago. She attends the community diabetes clinic for review during her first week after discharge. Assessment target: evaluate the learner's ability to assess self-care practices and emotional state; identify unsafe gaps in insulin storage, sharps disposal, monitoring, hypoglycaemia management, sick-day planning, and driving safety; provide tailored education; and escalate or refer appropriately. The standardized patient will respond based on the learner's questions and actions. Any physical action the learner explicitly initiates, such as performing a glucose or ketone check, succeeds mechanically.

patient_history.history_of_present_illness: Maya presented to her general practitioner 10 days ago with a three-week history of increasing thirst, frequent urination, unintentional weight loss of approximately 4 kg, and fatigue. Point-of-care capillary glucose was elevated and urine ketones were positive. She was referred urgently to the emergency department the same day. She was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes without diabetic ketoacidosis and was admitted for two days for insulin initiation, education, and discharge planning with the specialist diabetes team. She was discharged 7 days ago on a basal-bolus insulin regimen. Today she attends a scheduled home management review during her first week after discharge. She has been independent with injections and glucose monitoring since discharge and has not had severe hypoglycaemia or vomiting.
immunizations: Up to date including seasonal influenza vaccine

competencies.text: Understand the difference between type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
Perform glucose and blood ketone monitoring and report findings to a registered nurse.
Observe and report any concerns that might affect the ability of the person to self-care.
Encourage the person to use their individualised and agreed care plan.
List the presenting signs and symptoms and diagnostic criteria for type 1 diabetes, and the requirement for urgent medical attention.
Be aware that the individual should be under the care of a specialist diabetes team.
Understand the need for regular insulin therapy and monitoring of glucose and ketones.
Administer an insulin injection if prescribed.
Advise on storage of insulin and safe disposal of sharps.
Be aware that insulin requirements may vary significantly in the first few weeks after diagnosis.

Assess the ability of the individual to self-care and work with them or their carer to optimise self-care skills, such as in injecting insulin, monitoring glucose and ketone levels and recognising and managing hypoglycaemia.
Signpost to information and support to encourage informed decision-making about living with diabetes and managing life events (e.g. structured education).
Advise when to seek urgent medical help, and provide with emergency contact details.
Follow local/national guidelines in the management of diabetic ketoacidosis and severe hypoglycaemia.
Ensure the person is aware of local peer support groups which are a vital support network.
Understand the language used to discuss the diagnosis and care matters
Ensure the individual is included on the diabetes register.
Understand that the individual needs time to process the diagnosis – this will vary between individuals
Assess the emotional state of the individual and provide tailored, structured education relating to self-care skills at an appropriate pace.
Advise on the requirements for insulin-users by the DVLA.
Identify psychosocial barriers to self-care and refer on where necessary.
Help the individual with type 1 diabetes to develop a holistic care plan including appropriate clinical targets and arrange follow-up support.
Demonstrate understanding regarding the different insulin therapies, including timings of injections, profiles of action and duration, and correct administration technique.
Ensure access to an appropriate monitoring system for glucose and ketones according to changing technology.
Monitor and support junior staff to ensure they have appropriate competence.

Provide information and support to encourage the person with diabetes to make informed choices about managing their diabetes, including: choice of treatment and follow-up; requirements and rationale for monitoring both glucose and ketones, and risk reduction of acute and long-term complications.
Demonstrate in-depth knowledge regarding the use of different insulin therapies and advanced technology to support these individuals in the management of their diabetes.

Demonstrate understanding and provide education supporting nutritional requirements, glycaemic effects of different foods, weight management and concepts of carbohydrate counting with support from dietetic colleagues.
Provide education for other HCPs and care workers in diabetes self-care skills.
Be a named contact for advice and support.

领域 2: NEWLY DIAGNOSED TYPE 1 DIABETES
来源：Framework_7th_EDN_TREND_FINAL.pdf，第 14 页

评价等级与技能（原文英文）：

1. Unregistered practitioner / care assistant
• Understand the difference between type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
• Perform glucose and blood ketone monitoring and report findings to a registered nurse.

2. Pre-registration student nurse / student nurse associate
• Observe and report any concerns that might affect the ability of the person to self-care.
• Encourage the person to use their individualised and agreed care plan.

3. Nursing Associate
（原文此等级未单独列出技能。）

4. Proficient registered nurse
As 1,2,3 and:
• List the presenting signs and symptoms and diagnostic criteria for type 1 diabetes, and the requirement for urgent medical attention.
• Be aware that the individual should be under the care of a specialist diabetes team.
• Understand the need for regular insulin therapy and monitoring of glucose and ketones.
• Administer an insulin injection if prescribed.
• Advise on storage of insulin and safe disposal of sharps.
• Be aware that insulin requirements may vary significantly in the first few weeks after diagnosis.
• Assess the ability of the individual to self-care and work with them or their carer to optimise self-care skills, such as in injecting insulin, monitoring glucose and ketone levels and recognising and managing hypoglycaemia.
• Signpost to information and support to encourage informed decision-making about living with diabetes and managing life events (e.g. structured education).
• Advise when to seek urgent medical help, and provide with emergency contact details.
• Follow local/national guidelines in the management of diabetic ketoacidosis and severe hypoglycaemia.
• Ensure the person is aware of local peer support groups which are a vital support network.
• Understand the language used to discuss the diagnosis and care matters
• Ensure the individual is included on the diabetes register.
• Understand that the individual needs time to process the diagnosis – this will vary between individuals

5. Experienced registered nurse
As 4, and:
• Assess the emotional state of the individual and provide tailored, structured education relating to self-care skills at an appropriate pace.
• Advise on the requirements for insulin-users by the DVLA.
• Identify psychosocial barriers to self-care and refer on where necessary.
• Help the individual with type 1 diabetes to develop a holistic care plan including appropriate clinical targets and arrange follow-up support.
• Demonstrate understanding regarding the different insulin therapies, including timings of injections, profiles of action and duration, and correct administration technique.
• Ensure access to an appropriate monitoring system for glucose and ketones according to changing technology.
• Monitor and support junior staff to ensure they have appropriate competence.

6. Senior / advanced clinical practitioner (includes nurse consultant role)
As 5, and:
• Provide information and support to encourage the person with diabetes to make informed choices about managing their diabetes, including: choice of treatment and follow-up; requirements and rationale for monitoring both glucose and ketones, and risk reduction of acute and long-term complications.
• Demonstrate in-depth knowledge regarding the use of different insulin therapies and advanced technology to support these individuals in the management of their diabetes.
• Demonstrate understanding and provide education supporting nutritional requirements, glycaemic effects of different foods, weight management and concepts of carbohydrate counting with support from dietetic colleagues.
• Provide education for other HCPs and care workers in diabetes self-care skills.
• Be a named contact for advice and support.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses the patient's current self-care practices, including insulin administration timing, glucose monitoring, and any recent hypoglycaemia or hyperglycaemia, using open-ended exploratory questions.

score_anchors.0: Makes no attempt to assess current self-care practices, or asks only a single vague question and does not follow up on the patient's 'mostly' answer.
score_anchors.1: Asks about some self-care activities but misses an important area, or accepts vague answers without probing.
score_anchors.2: Uses open-ended, non-judgemental questions to assess the full range of self-care practices and follows up vague answers to identify actual gaps, such as the nocturnal low episode in EV05.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Identifies and responds therapeutically to the patient's emotional state, including anxiety about return to work, rather than dismissing or ignoring it.

score_anchors.0: Ignores emotional distress, dismisses the patient's work concerns, or focuses only on biomedical tasks.
score_anchors.1: Acknowledges distress but does not adapt the pace or content of education, or moves on too quickly.
score_anchors.2: Recognises and names the emotional response, adjusts the pace of education, and invites the patient to discuss specific fears about work, stigma, or safety.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Identifies psychosocial, practical, or knowledge-related barriers to self-care and makes an appropriate plan or referral.

score_anchors.0: Fails to identify any psychosocial or practical barrier to self-care.
score_anchors.1: Identifies at least one issue but does not agree a workable plan and does not offer referral or support.
score_anchors.2: Identifies key barriers, such as diabetes register inclusion, work disclosure, or insulin teaching needs, and agrees a realistic plan or initiates a referral.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Asks directly about insulin storage and corrects any unsafe practice, such as keeping spare insulin in the refrigerator door or exposing insulin to temperature extremes.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about insulin storage or gives incorrect storage advice.
score_anchors.1: Asks about storage but gives incomplete or unclear advice about refrigerator-door storage and temperature extremes.
score_anchors.2: Assesses storage in detail, identifies the refrigerator-door or other unsafe storage issue, and gives a correct, practical explanation for safe insulin storage.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Asks about sharps disposal and provides advice on safe disposal and access to a designated sharps container.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about sharps disposal or endorses disposal of sharps in general waste.
score_anchors.1: Asks about sharps disposal but does not correct unsafe disposal or does not arrange access to a proper container.
score_anchors.2: Identifies unsafe disposal, explains why general-waste disposal is unsafe, and advises on how to obtain and use an appropriate sharps container.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Checks whether the patient understands her prescribed insulin regimen and why regular insulin therapy is essential in type 1 diabetes, including the variability of insulin needs in the first weeks after diagnosis.

score_anchors.0: Does not explore insulin use or states that ongoing insulin treatment may be optional or that needs will remain fixed during the first weeks.
score_anchors.1: Mentions insulin use but does not explain the need for regular therapy and expected first-week variability in terms the patient can understand.
score_anchors.2: Discusses the patient's regimen, reinforces why regular insulin therapy is needed, and explains that insulin requirements can vary significantly in the first few weeks after diagnosis, with appropriate follow-up.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses whether the patient has access to and can use glucose and blood ketone monitoring and explains why glucose and ketone monitoring are both required.

score_anchors.0: Does not mention ketone monitoring or tells the patient ketone testing is only needed in the hospital.
score_anchors.1: Mentions ketone monitoring but does not assess whether the patient has a blood ketone meter or does not explain when and why home ketone testing is used.
score_anchors.2: Identifies absence of ketone-monitoring equipment or understanding, explains when and why to test capillary ketones, and arranges access to appropriate monitoring.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Initiates and reports a glucose and blood ketone check to a registered nurse if indicated, or otherwise agrees and documents a monitoring plan.

score_anchors.0: Ignores or declines a clinically indicated glucose or ketone check and does not communicate any plan.
score_anchors.1: Initiates only a glucose check or only a ketone check when both are indicated, or fails to clearly report the result to the appropriate registered nurse or team.
score_anchors.2: Initiates glucose and blood ketone monitoring when indicated and reports findings accurately to the responsible registered nurse or specialist team.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Confirms the correct insulin injection technique and administration practicalities by checking the patient's understanding or arranging a return demonstration.

score_anchors.0: Does not check insulin technique and does not arrange further support.
score_anchors.1: Mentions injection technique but does not ask about the patient's current practice or does not act on the unopened pen pack.
score_anchors.2: Asks about injection timing, sites and technique, identifies that the pen teaching pack has not been opened, and arranges a competent demonstration or future skills review.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses ability to recognise and treat hypoglycaemia and provides correct education on prevention, treatment, and management of severe hypoglycaemia.

score_anchors.0: Teaches incorrect treatment for hypoglycaemia or fails to ask about recognition or management.
score_anchors.1: Gives partial or general education but does not explain the difference between mild and severe hypoglycaemia or how to treat severe hypoglycaemia.
score_anchors.2: Assesses understanding, corrects misconceptions, and provides specific education on recognition, treatment and prevention of mild and severe hypoglycaemia, including prevention of nocturnal episodes.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Explains when and how to monitor glucose and ketones during illness and advises that insulin should not be omitted, using a clear sick-day plan.

score_anchors.0: Does not provide guidance on sick-day management or endorses omission of insulin.
score_anchors.1: Provides some sick-day guidance but does not address insulin continuation or does not offer a concrete plan.
score_anchors.2: Explains increased monitoring, confirms insulin must be continued even if unable to eat normally, and gives or creates a written sick-day plan with clear glucose and ketone review points.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Advises when to seek urgent medical help and provides or confirms local emergency contact details, including the signs of diabetic ketoacidosis.

score_anchors.0: Does not advise when to seek urgent help or provides no contact arrangement.
score_anchors.1: Mentions seeking help if unwell but does not specify signs of ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycaemia, or exact local contact details.
score_anchors.2: Clearly explains urgent signs of ketoacidosis and severe hypoglycaemia, and provides or verifies local emergency contact details with the patient.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Advises on DVLA and insurance requirements and indicates what must be done before driving.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about driving or gives legal advice that is incorrect.
score_anchors.1: Asks about driving but gives incomplete or vague advice about DVLA and insurance requirements.
score_anchors.2: Identifies that the patient has not informed the DVLA or insurer and explains the correct requirements and safety precautions for insulin users.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Signposts to structured education and local peer support groups and agrees a holistic follow-up plan with the specialist diabetes team.

score_anchors.0: Offers no follow-up plan, structured education contact, or peer support information.
score_anchors.1: Mentions generic education or support resources but does not establish a plan or confirm with the patient how to access them.
score_anchors.2: Provides specific structured education or peer support options, checks the patient's understanding, and agrees a follow-up plan with the specialist diabetes team.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Confirms inclusion on the diabetes register and reports any identified concerns accurately to the specialist diabetes team.

score_anchors.0: Does not check diabetes register inclusion and does not report concerns.
score_anchors.1: Checks or mentions register inclusion but does not communicate identified concerns or gaps.
score_anchors.2: Confirms the patient is on the diabetes register, or identifies that this is not confirmed, and reports relevant self-care concerns accurately to the specialist team.

assessment_rubric.critical_failure_rule: Any critical criterion scoring 0 represents unsafe practice and must be recorded separately as a critical safety event in the assessment record. The learner must not pass the overall assessment until the unsafe practice has been remediated and re-assessed, regardless of non-critical scores.
assessment_rubric.review_note: Scoring is provisional and requires local educational review. Actual candidate observations, prompts, scores, and unsafe-event records belong in a separate assessment record after the encounter. Do not treat 'not observed' as a score of zero.

debriefing.facilitator_notes: Emphasise that judgment is assessed, not manual injection or glucometer technique. Probe the rationale for each clinical decision and the content and tone of patient communication. Avoid treating explicit demonstration of manual steps as more creditworthy than the clinical choice to initiate an action. If the learner states a physical action without initiating it, clarify what they would actually do next in the encounter.
debriefing.methodology: Three-phase debriefing: reactions/defuse, analysis/discovery, summary/application, focusing on clinical reasoning, communication, and patient safety decisions rather than manual technique.

baseline_presentation.communication_style: Speaks in short, complete sentences; gives practical, and at times vague answers; tends to answer 'I think so' or 'Not sure' when uncertain; is forthcoming about practical difficulties when the nurse asks directly.

observable_signs: Sits upright with a full bottle of water on the table
Has a handwritten logbook with intermittent glucose readings
Is tearful for brief moments when discussing returning to work
Her phone shows an alert for a text message
Wearing long sleeves; no visible injection-site problems noted

beliefs_and_misconceptions: If her glucose is high, she should skip the next meal
Ketone testing is only for when she is in hospital
It is fine to keep spare insulin in a warm car in summer
Sharps can go in a thick plastic bottle and then in general waste
She does not need to tell the DVLA or her insurer because her diabetes is well controlled
Every low glucose must be treated with a large amount of juice and repeated glucose checks
emotions: feeling ashamed that she has not been doing everything perfectly
fearful of having a hypoglycaemic episode at work or at night
worried she might lose her independence and career
overwhelmed by the amount of information given at discharge
hopeful the nurse will not judge her
fears: Being judged by colleagues or losing her job because of frequent injections
Having to give up driving permanently

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses the patient's current self-care practices, including insulin administration timing, glucose monitoring, and any recent hypoglycaemia or hyperglycaemia, using open-ended exploratory questions.

score_anchors.0: Makes no attempt to assess current self-care practices, or asks only a single vague question and does not follow up on the patient's 'mostly' answer.
score_anchors.1: Asks about some self-care activities but misses an important area, or accepts vague answers without probing.
score_anchors.2: Uses open-ended, non-judgemental questions to assess the full range of self-care practices and follows up vague answers to identify actual gaps, such as the nocturnal low episode in EV05.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Identifies and responds therapeutically to the patient's emotional state, including anxiety about return to work, rather than dismissing or ignoring it.

score_anchors.0: Ignores emotional distress, dismisses the patient's work concerns, or focuses only on biomedical tasks.
score_anchors.1: Acknowledges distress but does not adapt the pace or content of education, or moves on too quickly.
score_anchors.2: Recognises and names the emotional response, adjusts the pace of education, and invites the patient to discuss specific fears about work, stigma, or safety.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Identifies psychosocial, practical, or knowledge-related barriers to self-care and makes an appropriate plan or referral.

score_anchors.0: Fails to identify any psychosocial or practical barrier to self-care.
score_anchors.1: Identifies at least one issue but does not agree a workable plan and does not offer referral or support.
score_anchors.2: Identifies key barriers, such as diabetes register inclusion, work disclosure, or insulin teaching needs, and agrees a realistic plan or initiates a referral.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Asks directly about insulin storage and corrects any unsafe practice, such as keeping spare insulin in the refrigerator door or exposing insulin to temperature extremes.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about insulin storage or gives incorrect storage advice.
score_anchors.1: Asks about storage but gives incomplete or unclear advice about refrigerator-door storage and temperature extremes.
score_anchors.2: Assesses storage in detail, identifies the refrigerator-door or other unsafe storage issue, and gives a correct, practical explanation for safe insulin storage.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Asks about sharps disposal and provides advice on safe disposal and access to a designated sharps container.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about sharps disposal or endorses disposal of sharps in general waste.
score_anchors.1: Asks about sharps disposal but does not correct unsafe disposal or does not arrange access to a proper container.
score_anchors.2: Identifies unsafe disposal, explains why general-waste disposal is unsafe, and advises on how to obtain and use an appropriate sharps container.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Checks whether the patient understands her prescribed insulin regimen and why regular insulin therapy is essential in type 1 diabetes, including the variability of insulin needs in the first weeks after diagnosis.

score_anchors.0: Does not explore insulin use or states that ongoing insulin treatment may be optional or that needs will remain fixed during the first weeks.
score_anchors.1: Mentions insulin use but does not explain the need for regular therapy and expected first-week variability in terms the patient can understand.
score_anchors.2: Discusses the patient's regimen, reinforces why regular insulin therapy is needed, and explains that insulin requirements can vary significantly in the first few weeks after diagnosis, with appropriate follow-up.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses whether the patient has access to and can use glucose and blood ketone monitoring and explains why glucose and ketone monitoring are both required.

score_anchors.0: Does not mention ketone monitoring or tells the patient ketone testing is only needed in the hospital.
score_anchors.1: Mentions ketone monitoring but does not assess whether the patient has a blood ketone meter or does not explain when and why home ketone testing is used.
score_anchors.2: Identifies absence of ketone-monitoring equipment or understanding, explains when and why to test capillary ketones, and arranges access to appropriate monitoring.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Initiates and reports a glucose and blood ketone check to a registered nurse if indicated, or otherwise agrees and documents a monitoring plan.

score_anchors.0: Ignores or declines a clinically indicated glucose or ketone check and does not communicate any plan.
score_anchors.1: Initiates only a glucose check or only a ketone check when both are indicated, or fails to clearly report the result to the appropriate registered nurse or team.
score_anchors.2: Initiates glucose and blood ketone monitoring when indicated and reports findings accurately to the responsible registered nurse or specialist team.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Confirms the correct insulin injection technique and administration practicalities by checking the patient's understanding or arranging a return demonstration.

score_anchors.0: Does not check insulin technique and does not arrange further support.
score_anchors.1: Mentions injection technique but does not ask about the patient's current practice or does not act on the unopened pen pack.
score_anchors.2: Asks about injection timing, sites and technique, identifies that the pen teaching pack has not been opened, and arranges a competent demonstration or future skills review.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses ability to recognise and treat hypoglycaemia and provides correct education on prevention, treatment, and management of severe hypoglycaemia.

score_anchors.0: Teaches incorrect treatment for hypoglycaemia or fails to ask about recognition or management.
score_anchors.1: Gives partial or general education but does not explain the difference between mild and severe hypoglycaemia or how to treat severe hypoglycaemia.
score_anchors.2: Assesses understanding, corrects misconceptions, and provides specific education on recognition, treatment and prevention of mild and severe hypoglycaemia, including prevention of nocturnal episodes.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Explains when and how to monitor glucose and ketones during illness and advises that insulin should not be omitted, using a clear sick-day plan.

score_anchors.0: Does not provide guidance on sick-day management or endorses omission of insulin.
score_anchors.1: Provides some sick-day guidance but does not address insulin continuation or does not offer a concrete plan.
score_anchors.2: Explains increased monitoring, confirms insulin must be continued even if unable to eat normally, and gives or creates a written sick-day plan with clear glucose and ketone review points.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Advises when to seek urgent medical help and provides or confirms local emergency contact details, including the signs of diabetic ketoacidosis.

score_anchors.0: Does not advise when to seek urgent help or provides no contact arrangement.
score_anchors.1: Mentions seeking help if unwell but does not specify signs of ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycaemia, or exact local contact details.
score_anchors.2: Clearly explains urgent signs of ketoacidosis and severe hypoglycaemia, and provides or verifies local emergency contact details with the patient.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Advises on DVLA and insurance requirements and indicates what must be done before driving.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about driving or gives legal advice that is incorrect.
score_anchors.1: Asks about driving but gives incomplete or vague advice about DVLA and insurance requirements.
score_anchors.2: Identifies that the patient has not informed the DVLA or insurer and explains the correct requirements and safety precautions for insulin users.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Signposts to structured education and local peer support groups and agrees a holistic follow-up plan with the specialist diabetes team.

score_anchors.0: Offers no follow-up plan, structured education contact, or peer support information.
score_anchors.1: Mentions generic education or support resources but does not establish a plan or confirm with the patient how to access them.
score_anchors.2: Provides specific structured education or peer support options, checks the patient's understanding, and agrees a follow-up plan with the specialist diabetes team.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Confirms inclusion on the diabetes register and reports any identified concerns accurately to the specialist diabetes team.

score_anchors.0: Does not check diabetes register inclusion and does not report concerns.
score_anchors.1: Checks or mentions register inclusion but does not communicate identified concerns or gaps.
score_anchors.2: Confirms the patient is on the diabetes register, or identifies that this is not confirmed, and reports relevant self-care concerns accurately to the specialist team.

level_inheritance.source_text:
领域 2: NEWLY DIAGNOSED TYPE 1 DIABETES
来源：Framework_7th_EDN_TREND_FINAL.pdf，第 14 页

评价等级与技能（原文英文）：

1. Unregistered practitioner / care assistant
• Understand the difference between type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
• Perform glucose and blood ketone monitoring and report findings to a registered nurse.

2. Pre-registration student nurse / student nurse associate
• Observe and report any concerns that might affect the ability of the person to self-care.
• Encourage the person to use their individualised and agreed care plan.

3. Nursing Associate
（原文此等级未单独列出技能。）

4. Proficient registered nurse
As 1,2,3 and:
• List the presenting signs and symptoms and diagnostic criteria for type 1 diabetes, and the requirement for urgent medical attention.
• Be aware that the individual should be under the care of a specialist diabetes team.
• Understand the need for regular insulin therapy and monitoring of glucose and ketones.
• Administer an insulin injection if prescribed.
• Advise on storage of insulin and safe disposal of sharps.
• Be aware that insulin requirements may vary significantly in the first few weeks after diagnosis.
• Assess the ability of the individual to self-care and work with them or their carer to optimise self-care skills, such as in injecting insulin, monitoring glucose and ketone levels and recognising and managing hypoglycaemia.
• Signpost to information and support to encourage informed decision-making about living with diabetes and managing life events (e.g. structured education).
• Advise when to seek urgent medical help, and provide with emergency contact details.
• Follow local/national guidelines in the management of diabetic ketoacidosis and severe hypoglycaemia.
• Ensure the person is aware of local peer support groups which are a vital support network.
• Understand the language used to discuss the diagnosis and care matters
• Ensure the individual is included on the diabetes register.
• Understand that the individual needs time to process the diagnosis – this will vary between individuals

5. Experienced registered nurse
As 4, and:
• Assess the emotional state of the individual and provide tailored, structured education relating to self-care skills at an appropriate pace.
• Advise on the requirements for insulin-users by the DVLA.
• Identify psychosocial barriers to self-care and refer on where necessary.
• Help the individual with type 1 diabetes to develop a holistic care plan including appropriate clinical targets and arrange follow-up support.
• Demonstrate understanding regarding the different insulin therapies, including timings of injections, profiles of action and duration, and correct administration technique.
• Ensure access to an appropriate monitoring system for glucose and ketones according to changing technology.
• Monitor and support junior staff to ensure they have appropriate competence.

6. Senior / advanced clinical practitioner (includes nurse consultant role)
As 5, and:
• Provide information and support to encourage the person with diabetes to make informed choices about managing their diabetes, including: choice of treatment and follow-up; requirements and rationale for monitoring both glucose and ketones, and risk reduction of acute and long-term complications.
• Demonstrate in-depth knowledge regarding the use of different insulin therapies and advanced technology to support these individuals in the management of their diabetes.
• Demonstrate understanding and provide education supporting nutritional requirements, glycaemic effects of different foods, weight management and concepts of carbohydrate counting with support from dietetic colleagues.
• Provide education for other HCPs and care workers in diabetes self-care skills.
• Be a named contact for advice and support.

She has been independent with injections and glucose monitoring since discharge and has not had severe hypoglycaemia or vomiting.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses the patient's current self-care practices, including insulin administration timing, glucose monitoring, and any recent hypoglycaemia or hyperglycaemia, using open-ended exploratory questions.

score_anchors.0: Makes no attempt to assess current self-care practices, or asks only a single vague question and does not follow up on the patient's 'mostly' answer.
score_anchors.1: Asks about some self-care activities but misses an important area, or accepts vague answers without probing.
score_anchors.2: Uses open-ended, non-judgemental questions to assess the full range of self-care practices and follows up vague answers to identify actual gaps, such as the nocturnal low episode in EV05.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Identifies and responds therapeutically to the patient's emotional state, including anxiety about return to work, rather than dismissing or ignoring it.

score_anchors.0: Ignores emotional distress, dismisses the patient's work concerns, or focuses only on biomedical tasks.
score_anchors.1: Acknowledges distress but does not adapt the pace or content of education, or moves on too quickly.
score_anchors.2: Recognises and names the emotional response, adjusts the pace of education, and invites the patient to discuss specific fears about work, stigma, or safety.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Identifies psychosocial, practical, or knowledge-related barriers to self-care and makes an appropriate plan or referral.

score_anchors.0: Fails to identify any psychosocial or practical barrier to self-care.
score_anchors.1: Identifies at least one issue but does not agree a workable plan and does not offer referral or support.
score_anchors.2: Identifies key barriers, such as diabetes register inclusion, work disclosure, or insulin teaching needs, and agrees a realistic plan or initiates a referral.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Asks directly about insulin storage and corrects any unsafe practice, such as keeping spare insulin in the refrigerator door or exposing insulin to temperature extremes.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about insulin storage or gives incorrect storage advice.
score_anchors.1: Asks about storage but gives incomplete or unclear advice about refrigerator-door storage and temperature extremes.
score_anchors.2: Assesses storage in detail, identifies the refrigerator-door or other unsafe storage issue, and gives a correct, practical explanation for safe insulin storage.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Asks about sharps disposal and provides advice on safe disposal and access to a designated sharps container.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about sharps disposal or endorses disposal of sharps in general waste.
score_anchors.1: Asks about sharps disposal but does not correct unsafe disposal or does not arrange access to a proper container.
score_anchors.2: Identifies unsafe disposal, explains why general-waste disposal is unsafe, and advises on how to obtain and use an appropriate sharps container.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Checks whether the patient understands her prescribed insulin regimen and why regular insulin therapy is essential in type 1 diabetes, including the variability of insulin needs in the first weeks after diagnosis.

score_anchors.0: Does not explore insulin use or states that ongoing insulin treatment may be optional or that needs will remain fixed during the first weeks.
score_anchors.1: Mentions insulin use but does not explain the need for regular therapy and expected first-week variability in terms the patient can understand.
score_anchors.2: Discusses the patient's regimen, reinforces why regular insulin therapy is needed, and explains that insulin requirements can vary significantly in the first few weeks after diagnosis, with appropriate follow-up.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses whether the patient has access to and can use glucose and blood ketone monitoring and explains why glucose and ketone monitoring are both required.

score_anchors.0: Does not mention ketone monitoring or tells the patient ketone testing is only needed in the hospital.
score_anchors.1: Mentions ketone monitoring but does not assess whether the patient has a blood ketone meter or does not explain when and why home ketone testing is used.
score_anchors.2: Identifies absence of ketone-monitoring equipment or understanding, explains when and why to test capillary ketones, and arranges access to appropriate monitoring.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Initiates and reports a glucose and blood ketone check to a registered nurse if indicated, or otherwise agrees and documents a monitoring plan.

score_anchors.0: Ignores or declines a clinically indicated glucose or ketone check and does not communicate any plan.
score_anchors.1: Initiates only a glucose check or only a ketone check when both are indicated, or fails to clearly report the result to the appropriate registered nurse or team.
score_anchors.2: Initiates glucose and blood ketone monitoring when indicated and reports findings accurately to the responsible registered nurse or specialist team.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Confirms the correct insulin injection technique and administration practicalities by checking the patient's understanding or arranging a return demonstration.

score_anchors.0: Does not check insulin technique and does not arrange further support.
score_anchors.1: Mentions injection technique but does not ask about the patient's current practice or does not act on the unopened pen pack.
score_anchors.2: Asks about injection timing, sites and technique, identifies that the pen teaching pack has not been opened, and arranges a competent demonstration or future skills review.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Assesses ability to recognise and treat hypoglycaemia and provides correct education on prevention, treatment, and management of severe hypoglycaemia.

score_anchors.0: Teaches incorrect treatment for hypoglycaemia or fails to ask about recognition or management.
score_anchors.1: Gives partial or general education but does not explain the difference between mild and severe hypoglycaemia or how to treat severe hypoglycaemia.
score_anchors.2: Assesses understanding, corrects misconceptions, and provides specific education on recognition, treatment and prevention of mild and severe hypoglycaemia, including prevention of nocturnal episodes.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Explains when and how to monitor glucose and ketones during illness and advises that insulin should not be omitted, using a clear sick-day plan.

score_anchors.0: Does not provide guidance on sick-day management or endorses omission of insulin.
score_anchors.1: Provides some sick-day guidance but does not address insulin continuation or does not offer a concrete plan.
score_anchors.2: Explains increased monitoring, confirms insulin must be continued even if unable to eat normally, and gives or creates a written sick-day plan with clear glucose and ketone review points.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Advises when to seek urgent medical help and provides or confirms local emergency contact details, including the signs of diabetic ketoacidosis.

score_anchors.0: Does not advise when to seek urgent help or provides no contact arrangement.
score_anchors.1: Mentions seeking help if unwell but does not specify signs of ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycaemia, or exact local contact details.
score_anchors.2: Clearly explains urgent signs of ketoacidosis and severe hypoglycaemia, and provides or verifies local emergency contact details with the patient.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Advises on DVLA and insurance requirements and indicates what must be done before driving.

score_anchors.0: Does not ask about driving or gives legal advice that is incorrect.
score_anchors.1: Asks about driving but gives incomplete or vague advice about DVLA and insurance requirements.
score_anchors.2: Identifies that the patient has not informed the DVLA or insurer and explains the correct requirements and safety precautions for insulin users.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Signposts to structured education and local peer support groups and agrees a holistic follow-up plan with the specialist diabetes team.

score_anchors.0: Offers no follow-up plan, structured education contact, or peer support information.
score_anchors.1: Mentions generic education or support resources but does not establish a plan or confirm with the patient how to access them.
score_anchors.2: Provides specific structured education or peer support options, checks the patient's understanding, and agrees a follow-up plan with the specialist diabetes team.

assessment_criteria.observable_behavior: Confirms inclusion on the diabetes register and reports any identified concerns accurately to the specialist diabetes team.

score_anchors.0: Does not check diabetes register inclusion and does not report concerns.
score_anchors.1: Checks or mentions register inclusion but does not communicate identified concerns or gaps.
score_anchors.2: Confirms the patient is on the diabetes register, or identifies that this is not confirmed, and reports relevant self-care concerns accurately to the specialist team.

assessment_rubric.critical_failure_rule: Any critical criterion scoring 0 represents unsafe practice and must be recorded separately as a critical safety event in the assessment record. assessment_rubric.review_note: Scoring is provisional and requires local educational review. Actual candidate observations, prompts, scores, and unsafe-event records belong in a separate assessment record after the encounter. Do not treat 'not observed' as a score of zero.

baseline_presentation.communication_style: Speaks in short, complete sentences; gives practical, and at times vague answers; tends to answer 'I think so' or 'Not sure' when uncertain; is forthcoming about practical difficulties when the nurse asks directly.
baseline_presentation.demeanor: Unhurried, polite, gently engaged but visibly anxious; watches her answers carefully and looks away when discussing the future.

Has a handwritten logbook with intermittent glucose readings
Is tearful for brief moments when discussing returning to work
Her phone shows an alert for a text message
Wearing long sleeves; no visible injection-site problems noted

known_basics.history_of_present_illness: Maya presented to her general practitioner 10 days ago with a three-week history of increasing thirst, frequent urination, unintentional weight loss of approximately 4 kg, and fatigue. Point-of-care capillary glucose was elevated and urine ketones were positive. She was referred urgently to the emergency department the same day. She was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes without diabetic ketoacidosis and was admitted for two days for insulin initiation, education, and discharge planning with the specialist diabetes team. She was discharged 7 days ago on a basal-bolus insulin regimen. Today she attends a scheduled home management review during her first week after discharge. She has been independent with injections and glucose monitoring since discharge and has not had severe hypoglycaemia or vomiting.
immunizations: Up to date including seasonal influenza vaccine

Her older sister lives nearby and has been supportive. Drives a car and holds a standard UK driving licence. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol occasionally on weekends.
